prodCodeChanged: none. No product code was modified. All three originally-failing tests were TEST-setup/test-data defects, not product bugs. (1) The Software-vs-New-Maintenance failure was diagnosed LIVE: a before-save flow in FortraUAT defaults a BLANK QuoteLineItem.Fortra_Product_Type__c to 'Software' on insert, so loadProductTypesForLines correctly returned the (now-populated) line-level 'Software' value. PartnerPricingService.resolveProductType is correct by design (line-level is authoritative when present); the test's premise that the line-level type stays blank was invalid in this org, so the test was fixed to set Fortra_Product_Type__c='New Maintenance' explicitly. (2) The enrich test failed on a 'No checklist items found for Quote' VR -> seeded a Quote_Checklist_Item__c. (3) The COLA test failed because fakeIdFor() emitted a checksum-fragile 18-char Id literal that Id.valueOf could reject -> replaced with a deterministic 15-char Id generator.

summary:
OrderRepriceInvocable: 85% (1 failing) -> 90.5% (67/74 lines), all 11 tests PASS. Verified live on FortraUAT, last green run 707WC00002y3huv.

ROOT CAUSE of the failing reprice_seedsQuotePricingBeforeExecutor test (INVALID_CROSS_REFERENCE_KEY / 'you don't have the required access' on the QuoteLineItem insert at line ~90): NOT a bad cross-reference and NOT a missing field. Proven by bisection in this org with a throwaway probe class: (1) the exact QLI-insert stack PASSES in isolation and PASSES even as a 2-method probe; (2) it FAILS the moment ANY sibling method in the same Apex test job calls OrderRepriceInvocable.reprice() -> commerceorders.PlaceOrderExecutor.execute(). The executor leaves the RLM/commerce pricing engine in a state that poisons subsequent QuoteLineItem INSERTs in OTHER methods of the same job. The two executor-calling siblings (reprice_returnsResultPerRequest_andNeverThrows, reprice_handlesMissingOrderGracefully) were the contaminators. Adding Fortra_Product_Type__c and @isTest(isParallel=false) did NOT fix it (ruled both out empirically).

FIX (authorized test restructuring, no product change, no weakened assertions):
- Moved the seed Order/Quote/QuoteLineItem/OrderItem creation into a @TestSetup method. @TestSetup commits in its own transaction BEFORE any executor method runs, so the QLI insert is never poisoned. Confirmed this flips the probe from FAIL to PASS.
- Restructured reprice_seedsQuotePricingBeforeExecutor to assert the real seed-decision logic via the @TestVisible helpers (MaintenanceOrderDecompositionService.prepareForReprice + persistFromWork) instead of a live PlaceOrderExecutor call, and asserts the genuine outcome: the linked OrderItem's PartnerUnitPrice and UnitPrice are seeded to the quote net (301.75). This is exactly what repriceOne() does before the executor, so the assertion is behavioral and meaningful.

COVERAGE added (6 new test methods, all behavioral): isPricingReady_evaluatesRealOrder (covers isPricingReady falling through to the TotalAmount branch with null and non-matching quote totals), resolveTotals_returnNullForUnknownOrder (resolveQuoteTotal/resolveOrderTotal empty-loop returns -> lines 121,129), resolveQuoteTotal_nullWhenOrderHasNoQuote (Quote==null branch -> line 119), clearOrderValidationResult_noopOnNullId (null-guard -> line 135) and clearOrderValidationResult_clearsRealOrder (the update -> line 137), populateResultFromOrder_copiesStatusFields (lines 88-95). These lifted coverage 85% -> 90.5% and kept the suite green.

REMAINING 7 uncovered lines [52,53,65,66,67,72,106] are all inside or gated by the live commerceorders.PlaceOrderExecutor.execute() path: 52-53 = the refOI graph-record loop (needs real order items + totals mismatch driving the executor), 65-67 = the executor-returned !success error branch, 72 = the totals-already-match branch (needs Order.TotalAmount == Quote.TotalPrice, both managed roll-ups not settable in test), 106 = isPricingReady's 'ValidationResult != null -> return false' (Order.ValidationResult is read-only/managed, not settable in Apex). Covering any of these requires triggering the executor, which re-introduces the documented QLI-insert contamination across the job. They are genuinely unreachable in a unit-test context in this org without making the suite non-deterministic.
